note: I rated scratchpad/w17 (m01-m19) and w17q (q01, q11, q19), 930x575, built from the w17 candidate (3ea3f24 + e6d3072 + fed7fdc in 10_mono.js), and diffed every frame pixel by pixel against scratchpad/w16 and w16q (script raterA17/diff.py; difference maps raterA17/d_*.png; side-by-side pairs raterA17/p_*.png and zooms raterA17/z_*.png). The monument changes show where expected: m04 (mean |diff| 6.9), m05 (6.1), m06, q11, m03, m16, m09, m01, m12, q19, m13, m17, m18, m08 and m14. The large m11 diff is the economy seat fabric (another area) and no monument in it changed. Sampling uses python3 + PIL, mean / p10 / p90 by luminance over boxes (x0,y0,x1,y1); the script is raterA17/samp.py. The candidate fixes most of the w16 list: the ash-wall frames now have rounded outer corners, stand proud, and carry darker clips straddling the top rail; the welcome head and tag sit above the monitor, and the latch is a horizontal oval with a thumb-turn in a D-boss; the bar has a flush nosing; the insert frames read and the cart handles are proud bars; the jump seats have flat webbing, buckles and a lap belt; the bassinet bar is gone; and the pots have more polish contrast. It also introduces three regressions. The welcome-glass glints read as two leaning sticks inside the cabinet, worst in m14. The switch to the ashDoor layer flattened the bar and ash-wall grain to about a third of the reference contrast, so the ash now reads as plain beige laminate. The new tumbler bodies are opaque mid-grey cups rather than dark clear glass. Lighting is noted but not scored: the galley top compartments are still washed out (m01, m09, m12, q19).

details.note: The flush nosing and full tumbler rims are improvements, but the nosing face is mid grey (L 140) where the render's is bright (L 230-240). The tumbler bodies are now opaque grey cups, and the bar doors lost their visible grain (std 3.3 against 6.5-9.8 in the render).

The head height, rounded tag and oval D-boss latch now match omaat_room_32. The new glass glints are hard lines that read as wires in m16 and as two leaning sticks in m14, and the head pokes about 1 cm above the recess ceiling in front of the black fascia.

The rounded proud frames and the clips straddling the top rail now match lalf_133. The ash is now nearly plain (std 3.2 against 9.2 in the photo). The lit and shadow strips are asymmetric: a dark line on one stile and a floating white sliver on the other.

issues.detail: Welcome-cabinet glass glints read as sticks (m14, m16, m03)
issues.problem: Two opaque, unlit diagonal quads (6 mm and 3 mm, #8e8c89 and #7a7876) sit on the pane. Up close they read as two wires across the shelves. From the J aisle (m14) they rasterise to 9 px and 4 px bars at about 2.4x the pane luminance, so the cabinet looks as if two rods are leaning inside it. The photo shows a soft, low-contrast sheen, not lines.
issues.evidence: m14 rows 220-260, x 400-450: the bars are at L 97 and 91 over a pane of 37-42 (raterA17/z_m14.png). In m16 there are two parallel lines across both shelves (raterA17/z_m16.png). omaat_room_32 shows a broad diffuse reflection only.
issues.fix: In buildWelcomeGalley in 10_mono.js, delete the two gQuad glints (the loop over [[0, 0.006, '#8e8c89'], [0.035, 0.003, '#7a7876']]). If a cue is still wanted, add one quad the size of the pane in front of it (cW - 0.1 by 0.67) and set its four vertex colours in the Builder so that only the upper-left corner is about 6-8 levels above the pane (around #3a3837) and the other three corners match the pane tone (#2b292a). That gives a soft gradient sheen with no edges.

issues.detail: Ash grain overcorrected on the bar, welcome and ash wall (q11, m04, m16)
issues.problem: Moving barAsh to LAYER.ashDoor removed the coarse banding but also nearly all of the grain. The bar doors and ash-wall flaps now read as plain beige laminate, while the render and the photo both show a clearly visible fine horizontal grain.
issues.evidence: q11 door (290,420,330,540) std 3.3 and m04 (150,250,370,500) std 3.2. samchui_render_11 doors have std 6.5-9.8 and lalf_133 has std 9.2 (raterA17/cmp_ash.png).
issues.fix: In 10_mono.js, give barAsh its own fine layer with roughly twice the ashDoor amplitude, or keep LAYER.ashDoor and darken the base so the grain shows: for example barAsh { c: '#b5a283', l: LAYER.ashDoor } plus a second barAshGrain with the ashGrain layer at half scale. If a layer amplitude has to change, do it with a one-line LAYER_PARAMS edit in 03_tex.js (a shared file) and aim for std 6-8 at m04.

issues.detail: Tumbler bodies are opaque grey cups (m05, m06, q11)
issues.problem: The rims are fixed, but the bodies are now a uniform matte #6a6e72, lighter than the render's dark clear glass. They read as grey tin or paper cups.
issues.evidence: m05 (205,430,300,455) #494d52 with p90 #848689, against samchui_render_11 (232,342,300,365) #383539. The render glasses show the black counter through them, with bright edge highlights on both sides (raterA17/r_tumb.png against raterA17/z_tumb.png).
issues.fix: In 10_mono.js, set MONMAT.tumbler back to about '#34363a' (r 0.05) and keep the full glassHi rim and base. Replace the single centre glint gQuad with two thin vertical glassHi quads at the left and right silhouettes (about ±0.027 in x, 0.004 wide), so each glass reads as clear and dark with bright edges.

issues.detail: Bar nosing front face is mid grey (m05, m06, q11)
issues.problem: The flush nosing is the right geometry, but under a 3 px bright lip its 45 mm face renders as a flat grey band (L 140). The render shows a bright satin band with a dark groove.
issues.evidence: m05 rows 516-532 are L 140 (#878a8f, std 7.4). samchui_render_11 rows 376-381 are L 235-243 and rows 387-395 are L 229-233.
issues.fix: In buildBar in 10_mono.js, tilt the nosing face slightly upward or split it into two gBoxes: a 20 mm upper band in steelBright, a 4 mm insertSeam groove, and a 20 mm lower band in steelBright with r about 0.2. Alternatively, give it a lighter material such as { c: '#e4e6e8', r: 0.25, m: 0.6 } so the vertical face is not left in the dark.

issues.detail: Ash-wall frame highlight strips are asymmetric (m04)
issues.problem: The lit and shadow quads are placed in local x, so on this aft-facing wall they mirror. One stile gets a dark inner line along its full height, and the other gets a white sliver 0.66 m long that floats mid-stile and stops short of the rounded corners. The two stiles therefore look like different parts.
issues.evidence: m04 at 4x (raterA17/c_m04tl_w17.png, raterA17/z_m04.png): a dark brown line runs down the left inner edge, and a white line on the right stile starts about 15 cm below the corner. In lalf_133 the lit edge runs continuously round the outer top and left of each frame.
issues.fix: In buildAshWall in 10_mono.js, drop the two vertical strips, or make them symmetric: put a lit outer strip of the full straight height (0.91 - 2 x 0.08) on both stiles and a single soft shadow strip only along the bottom inner edge. Keep the top lit strip.

issues.detail: Welcome head rises through the recess ceiling (m03)
issues.problem: The deeper top rail now reaches y 2.005, while the recess ceiling sits at 1.995 and the black fascia at 1.955-2.005. In m03 the head stands about 8 px above the fascia line as a separate lighter block.
issues.evidence: raterA17/z_m03head.png: the w17 head top is at about y 82, and the fascia top at about y 90.
issues.fix: In buildWelcomeGalley in 10_mono.js, make the top rail gBox(cW, 0.22, 0.03) at y 1.88 (top 1.99), and drop the tag to y 1.945 with the pictogram and text lines at 1.955 and 1.935.

issues.detail: Carry-over: door-1 dark wood streaks (q01, m19)
issues.problem: The fWood layer still shows radial streak aliasing at grazing angles.
issues.fix: In 10_mono.js, lower the darkWood and darkWoodDoor grain amplitude, or move them to a finer, lower-contrast layer for grazing views.

gapWorth03: Removing the hard welcome-glass glints (or replacing them with a soft vertex-colour sheen), restoring visible fine ash grain on barAsh (std about 6-8), and returning the tumblers to dark clear glass with edge highlights would each lift the welcome galley, the ash wall and the bar by about 0.2-0.3. That would take the area to about 8.6, with no detail below 8.3 except the lav doors (7.8).
